claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs is governed by lattice distortion induced primarily by the atomic-size mismatch of Al.
A critical Al concentration range exists in which accumulated lattice-strain energy offsets the ordering enthalpy that favors phase separation or precipitation.
The proposed strain–enthalpy balance stabilizes a disordered single-phase solid solution.
The stabilized single-phase alloy retains a combination of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
A near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy with low Al is a single-phase baseline below the ordering threshold.
The low-Al baseline has high configurational entropy and minimal lattice distortion.
Al concentration should be systematically increased while the Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni ratios and processing conditions are held nearly constant.
Lattice distortion can be tracked through X-ray-diffraction lattice-parameter shifts.
The onset of ordered precipitate formation can be observed by electron microscopy.
Measured lattice distortion and precipitate formation mediate the balance between configurational entropy and ordering tendencies.
Increasing Al to a moderate concentration increases lattice-strain energy because Al is larger than the other constituent atoms.
Moderate Al-induced lattice strain suppresses ordering and secondary-phase formation.
Above a critical Al concentration, excessive lattice strain promotes the nucleation of ordered precipitates.
The Al-associated ordered products may include B2 or L12 phases.
Al contents within the optimal range will remain disordered and single phase.
Al contents above the threshold will produce detectable ordered precipitates.
Ordered precipitation above the Al threshold may increase yield strength while reducing toughness or environmental resistance.
The mechanism applies to near-equiatomic Co–Cr–Fe–Ni matrices under conditions approaching equilibrium and may fail when rapid cooling or other nonequilibrium processing controls phase formation.
A lack of systematic correlation among Al concentration, measured lattice distortion, and ordered-phase emergence would falsify the hypothesis.
